questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere with beautiful nature as well as vibrant city vibes, and Vancouver had everything!

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit harder when I had to look for a place, as covid restrictions kept a lot of people in the city and reduced the supply of places to stay. But I found a place about a month before coming to Vancouver.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Vancouver is a big city and is very spread out, so you might end up spending a lot of time on a bus depending on where you decide to live. I lived right next to a Rapid Bus stop, which has made my life so much easier, so I would recommend looking at the distances and transportation to UBC before getting a place. That said, I really liked living off campus, as it made me feel more connected to the rest of Vancouver and was a nice break from the school environment. Also, housing in Vancouver is in general quite expensive!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit complicated - be prepared to do a lot of research on your own, especially if you have specific courses from KU you need to replace.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can do "course shopping" the first couple of weeks, which is really helpful in case you end up in a course that you aren't fond of. Courses were very limited at the time due to Covid, but if I wrote an email to the professors, they were very helpful with getting me into the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesful and got the courses I needed in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to try a lot of different courses in the beginning, so you end up taking the courses that you like the most. I found that every course really differed in quality depending on the instructors, so it's a good idea to try it out before you are locked into a course. Also, look at the course material/syllabus beforehand and see what kind of examination they do in the specific course - this really varies as well, and might impact how stressed you will be during exams!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses really varied in quality - I've had some of the best and some of the worst courses here!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were not very challenging, but required more work along the way (i.e. graded assignments, midterms, participation...). But I found that it was easy to keep up.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more like high school because you had to hand in smaller assignments along the way and you were graded for participation (but this is not the case in all of the courses). Also, it was more individualistic than at UCPH, and there were a lot of class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POLI 333A "Issues in Comparative Politics"
POLI 366 "International Political Economy"
SOCI 312 "Gender Relations"
GRSJ 300 "Intersectional Approaches to Thinking Gender"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would HIGHLY recommend SOCI312 "Gender Relations". It is the best course I have ever taken during my university years. Our instructor, Craig Meadows, is incredible, funny and extremely critical. I would recommend all courses with Craig Meadows.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was a part of VOC which is the UBC outdoor assocation, and they do many trips every weekend in nature that you can join. You can also rent equipment (for free - but with a deposit) which is super useful. I went on some of the most amazing hikes here. I was also a part of the Ski & Board Club, that hosted a really great Whistler Opening weekend. Would highly recommend!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: VOC (Varsity Outdoor Club) and Ski & Board Club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I bought a car with some other friends and we did trips every weekend. I would really recommend doing this! I can recommend Banff/Jasper, Gariabldi, Whistler, Vancouver Island, Mount Frosty (Especially in the last weekend of september), Hawaii, San Francisco, Unnecessary Mountain (yes, that's what it's called...)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! People are super nice and friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say yes to all invitations in the first few weeks. I found that these weeks were imperative for the people I have become close friends with today. This is the time when everyone is looking for new friends. And join in on some VOC hikes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There are ques to everything...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly Canadians are, the amazing nature and all the possibilities for great adventures in British Columbia. Campus is also really beautiful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Buy a Whistler Season pass and go skiing/boarding as often as possible. 
2) Get a car or an EVO membership so you have easy access to the outdoors and the beautiful nature around Vancouver. Just do as many trips as you can in general!
3) Allard Hall Library (Law building) is best for studying, there are mountain views!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The amazing people, the incredible nature and the beautiful city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid-19 restrictions on the application process and flights.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
